questions.q: What does COUNT() with empty parentheses count?
options: Every matching row, regardless of any field's null status
Only rows where the Id field is non-null
Nothing — COUNT() requires a field name argument
questions.explain: COUNT() behaves like COUNT(*) in standard SQL — it counts every matching row regardless of nulls in any particular field.

questions.q: If 500 contacts exist but only 420 have a non-null Email, what does COUNT(Email) return?
questions.explain: COUNT(fieldName) counts only rows where that specific field is not null — 420 contacts have an email on file.

questions.q: For an aggregate query with no GROUP BY, what Apex type does the query result come back as?
options: The object's own sObject type, e.g. List<Opportunity>
questions.explain: Aggregate queries without GROUP BY return AggregateResult, accessed by alias via .get('aliasName'), not the object's normal sObject type.

questions.q: When using MAX() on a picklist field, how is 'highest' determined?
options: MAX() cannot be used on picklist fields at all
Always alphabetically, regardless of picklist configuration
By the order values were most recently selected by users
By the picklist's configured sort order in Setup, not alphabetically
questions.explain: MIN and MAX on picklist fields use the picklist's defined value order from Setup, which may not match alphabetical order.

questions.q: Why is it good practice to alias an aggregate function, e.g. SUM(Amount) totalAmt?
options: It lets you retrieve the value by a readable name afterward, instead of a less readable auto-generated default
Aliasing is required syntax — a query fails to compile without it
Aliasing converts the result from AggregateResult into a normal sObject
Aliasing is only needed when using GROUP BY, never otherwise
questions.explain: Without an alias, Salesforce auto-generates a default name for the aggregate value; an explicit alias makes retrieving it by name in Apex clearer.
